title: Anne of Green Gables
author: L. M. Montgomery
short_summary: Anne Shirley is an imaginative, red-haired orphan mistakenly sent to elderly siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert, who had actually asked for a boy to help on their farm at Green Gables. Anne's talkative, dreamy nature quickly wins the Cuthberts over, and she grows up in the village of Avonlea on Prince Edward Island, making a bosom friend, a fierce rival, and a great many spectacular mistakes along the way.
extended_summary:
Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert send for an orphan boy to help on the farm and are given, instead, an eleven-year-old girl who talks without stopping, hates her red hair, and renames every pond and path she passes. Marilla means to send her back. She does not. Anne stays at Green Gables, grows up in Avonlea, and turns each ordinary year into a series of disasters and recoveries: she cracks her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head for calling her Carrots, accidentally gets her bosom friend Diana drunk on currant wine, saves a neighbour's baby from croup, flavours a cake with liniment, dyes her hair green, and falls off a roof on a dare.

Underneath the scrapes, the book is about being wanted. Anne earns a place in a household that did not ask for her, and in a village that first thought her strange. She grows into a serious student, wins a scholarship to college — and then, when Matthew dies suddenly and Marilla's sight begins to fail, gives it up to stay at Green Gables and teach nearby. The book ends with Anne making peace with Gilbert after years of rivalry, and deciding that a narrower road can still have flowers along it.

questions.prompt: Anne invites Diana to tea and serves her what she believes is raspberry cordial. What is actually in the bottle?

options: Marilla's three-year-old currant wine
Cold tea left over from the morning
Blackberry syrup meant for coughs
Vinegar that had been kept for pickling

questions.explanation: Anne pours it out in perfect innocence and Diana drinks three tumblerfuls. Mrs. Barry decides Anne got her daughter drunk on purpose and forbids the friendship — the first time Anne is punished for something she genuinely did not do, and it nearly breaks her heart.

questions.prompt: Anne brings her slate down on Gilbert Blythe's head on her first day of noticing him. What had he just done?

options: Pulled her braid and called her "Carrots"
Copied her answers during the spelling lesson
Told the class that she came from an orphanage
Said that girls should not be allowed at school

questions.explanation: Gilbert is only teasing, in the way boys tease girls they have noticed. But Anne's hair is the one thing she cannot bear to be laughed at about, and the slate is her answer. She then refuses to speak to him for about five years, which the book treats as both understandable and very funny.

questions.prompt: A peddler promises Anne that his dye will turn her red hair a beautiful raven black. Instead, her hair turns ___.
questions.explanation: No washing will shift it, and in the end Marilla has to cut the whole lot off. Anne, who has spent the entire book wishing her hair were any colour but red, discovers there is a colour she likes considerably less.

questions.prompt: Anne bakes a cake for the minister's wife and ruins it. What had she flavoured it with by mistake?

options: Anodyne liniment instead of vanilla
Salt instead of the caster sugar
Cooking soda instead of baking powder
Sour milk instead of the fresh cream

questions.explanation: Marilla had poured the leftover liniment into an old vanilla bottle. Anne is mortified, but Mrs. Allan laughs, eats a slice of something else, and becomes her friend — one of the book's quiet lessons about which adults are worth having.

questions.prompt: Anne gets into one scrape after another. Put them in the order they happen.

items: Anne cracks her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head
Diana is sent home tipsy after tea at Green Gables
Anne saves Minnie May Barry from croup in the night
The minister's wife is served a cake made with liniment
Anne falls off the Barrys' roof after accepting a dare
Anne's hair turns green and has to be cut off

questions.explanation: The order matters because Anne is growing up through it. The slate is pure temper; saving Minnie May is the first time the village sees she is useful; and by the green hair she can laugh at herself, which the eleven-year-old at the beginning could not have done.

questions.prompt: Match each person in Avonlea to what they do in Anne's story.

right: The neighbour who calls her plain and gets a furious apology
The teacher who prepares her for the entrance examination
The classmate whose dare puts her on a kitchen roof
The minister's wife who is kind about a ruined cake

questions.explanation: Avonlea is a whole village, not a backdrop. Two of these women make Anne worse and two make her better — and Mrs. Lynde, who begins as the enemy, ends up one of the people who defends her most fiercely.

questions.prompt: Anne renames everything she likes the look of. Sort each name into the right group.

content.groupB: What everyone else in Avonlea called it

options.label: The cherry tree outside the window

questions.explanation: Each pair is the same place twice: the pond, the road of apple trees, the cherry tree by her gable window. Renaming is how Anne takes possession of a place that did not want her at first — and by the end of the book the neighbours have started using her names too.

questions.prompt: Marilla's amethyst brooch goes missing and Anne is accused. Anne then confesses to losing it — although she had not touched it. Why does she confess?

options: She is told she cannot go to the picnic until she confesses
She wants to protect Diana, who had been in the room
She genuinely cannot remember whether she took it
She hopes Matthew will forgive her more quickly

questions.explanation: Anne invents a detailed confession purely to be allowed out to the picnic, which shocks Marilla more than the theft would have. The brooch turns up caught in Marilla's shawl, and it is Marilla who has to apologise — the first crack in her certainty that she always knows best.

questions.prompt: Anne wins a scholarship that would pay for four years at college. After Matthew dies and Marilla's eyesight begins to fail, Anne gives it up and stays at Green Gables to teach nearby. Was that the right decision, or should she have gone? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both answers can earn full marks. A strong 'right' answer notices that Marilla took Anne in when nobody else would, that she would have lost Green Gables alone, and that Anne says herself the road is only narrower, not worse. A strong 'should have gone' answer notices that Anne is sixteen, that the scholarship will not come again, and that Marilla never asked her to stay. Accept either, with a reason drawn from the book.

questions.prompt: Anne cannot leave a place with a dull name — a pond becomes the Lake of Shining Waters, a road of apple blossom becomes the White Way of Delight. Choose one ordinary place near where you live and give it a name Anne would approve of. What would you call it, and what about the place gave you the name?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer gives a name with some imagination in it and then explains what in the real place produced that name — the second half is what shows the child understood what Anne is doing. A name with no reason attached is a thinner answer.

questions.prompt: On the drive to Green Gables, Anne says her own name is not romantic enough and asks Matthew to call her ___ instead.
questions.explanation: She settles for her real name only on condition that it is spelled with an e, which she considers far more distinguished. It is our first warning that Anne will rename anything, including herself, if the given version is not beautiful enough.

questions.prompt: Anne and her friends act out a poem, with Anne floating downstream in a small flat-bottomed boat as the dead Lady of Shalott. What goes wrong?

options: The boat leaks and she has to cling to a bridge pile
The girls lose sight of her and raise the alarm too late
She drifts out into the harbour and cannot be reached
The boat overturns and she has to swim to the far bank

questions.explanation: The flat springs a leak, Anne scrambles onto a pile under the bridge and is left hanging there — and the person who rows past and rescues her is Gilbert Blythe. He asks to be friends; she refuses, and then regrets it for a long time afterwards.
